Want to create and sell digital products? Here's what you actually do. 👇  1. Start with a problem. What problem are you solving for someone else? The best digital products make something easier, faster, or less overwhelming. 2. Create the solution. Turn what you know into something useful—a guide, checklist, planner, workbook, template, printable, mini-course, or resource. 3. Choose where to sell it. You can sell digital products through platforms like Etsy, Teachers Pay Teachers, Stan Store, or your own website. Choose the platform that makes sense for your product and audience. You can also publish them on Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing or Google Play.  4. Market it. Creating the product is only HALF the job. People have to find it! Use Pinterest, TikTok,  email, a blog, or search-friendly content to show people how your product solves their problem. 5. Learn from the first one...then create another. Your first product doesn't have to build financial freedom. It's your starting point. Create one useful product. Learn how to sell it. Improve. Then create another. Over time, you can build a collection of digital products that can be purchased while you're teaching, spending time with family, or simply living your life. That's why you start that business. I know digital marketing, online business, and selling digital products can feel overwhelming when you don't understand how it all works. And with so many scams and people promising overnight success, I understand why some of you are hesitant. But hear me. If the Lord has placed something on your heart to create, don't automatically dismiss it because you don't understand the technology or the marketing. Maybe you know how to create meal plans that help busy families. Maybe you've learned how to prepare your household for emergencies. Maybe you've developed a system, a workbook, a checklist, or a resource that could help somebody else. That's knowledge. That's experience. And that could become a solution someone is willing to pay for. You don't have to manufacture a problem to sell a product. You identify a real need, create something useful, package it in a way people can understand, and learn how to get it in front of the people who need it. That's where digital marketing comes in. Now, does that mean every idea will sell? No. You still have to do your research, validate the need, and learn how to build responsibly. But don't let what you don't know stop you from learning what you need to know. Start with what God has already placed in your hands. Steward it well. Develop your skills. Serve people with excellence. And if you need help understanding how to turn your knowledge into a digital product and build the systems behind it, that's exactly the kind of work we do inside Biz Collective. Learn more at AngelicaStanley.co. #DigitalProducts #ChristianEntrepreneur #FaithBasedBusiness #DigitalMarketingForBeginners #bizcollective
